issues.legal_issue: An order for collecting profits from land in place of restoring possession cannot be made under the statutory alienation-remedy process unless the alienation has first been declared null and void.
material_facts: A holder of watan land sought a declaration that a permanent lease was null and void and sought possession of the land.
The initial authority rejected the application, and the appellate authority maintained that decision while ordering the tenant to pay additional rent.
Neither the Collector nor the Government declared the lease null and void.
issues.conclusion: The Collector had no jurisdiction to order additional rent under the statutory provision for collecting profits instead of transferring possession, because the lease had not been declared null and void. The Government’s later rent revision was not an order under that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9 of the Bombay Hereditary Offices Act, 1874, the Collector must first declare an alienation null and void before choosing between restoring possession and collecting the land’s profits in its place. Under section 9(2), collection of rent as profits follows that declaration and does not preserve the former lease as a tenancy. The Court did not decide whether the earlier High Court ruling had res judicata effect; it resolved the issue independently by interpreting section 9.

predicates.watan_alienation_proceeding: A holder of hereditary office sought relief concerning an alienation of land held as part of that office.
predicates.authority_rejected_invalidation_request: The authority refused to declare the alienation null and void.
predicates.authority_ordered_additional_rent_withou: The authority ordered the person in possession to pay additional rent without declaring the alienation null and void.
predicates.additional_rent_order_lacks_authority_as: An order for additional rent cannot operate as an authorized collection of profits following invalidation of the alienation.

issues.definition: When an alienation proceeding ends without a declaration invalidating the alienation, an additional-rent order cannot serve as an authorized post-invalidation collection of profits.

issues.legal_issue: A government rent revision that leaves a subsisting permanent lease in place operates as sanction for that lease at the revised rent, with its other terms unchanged.
material_facts: The original lease of watan land was permanent and fixed the rent.
After the holder of the land sought to invalidate the lease, the Government revised the rent but treated the person in possession as a tenant.
The Government did not declare the lease void, and the tenant continued in possession while paying the revised rent.
The Government’s order changed the rent but did not change the lease’s permanent character or the term that the rent would remain fixed.
issues.conclusion: The Government’s order operated under section 5 as sanction for a lease at the revised rent, rather than as action under section 9. The lease remained permanent, and its other terms remained unchanged.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Bombay Hereditary Offices Act, 1874, restricts a Watandar’s ability to lease watan land beyond the Watandar’s natural life without State Government sanction; by necessary implication, the Government may sanction such a lease. Section 9, by contrast, concerns declaring an alienation null and void and providing consequential relief. The Government’s treatment of the occupant as a tenant and its revision of rent, without invalidating the lease, supported the conclusion that it sanctioned the continuing lease with only the rent modified.

rule.if: watan_lease_sanction_proceeding and government_revised_rent_while_treating_occupant_as_tenant and government_did_not_invalidate_lease and lease_terms_were_otherwise_left_unchanged

predicates.watan_lease_sanction_proceeding: The matter concerned government approval of a lease of land held as part of a hereditary office.
predicates.government_revised_rent_while_treating_o: The Government revised the rent while treating the person in possession as a tenant.
predicates.government_did_not_invalidate_lease: The Government did not declare the lease null and void.
predicates.lease_terms_were_otherwise_left_unchange: The lease’s terms other than rent, including its permanent character, were left unchanged.
predicates.government_order_sanctions_continuing_le: The government order approves the continuing lease at the revised rent.

issues.definition: Where the Government revises rent while treating the occupant as a tenant, does not invalidate the lease, and leaves its other terms unchanged, the order sanctions the continuing lease at the revised rent.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord under a permanent lease with rent fixed by the lease as modified by government sanction cannot enhance the rent and is entitled only to the capitalized value of the rent when the leased land is compulsorily acquired.
material_facts: The land was held under a permanent lease whose rent was fixed and whose other terms remained unchanged after the Government revised the rent.
The landlord claimed a right to increase the rent, but the lease terms provided no such right.
Part of the leased land was compulsorily acquired, and the dispute concerned apportionment of the compensation between the landlord and the tenant.
issues.conclusion: The landlord had no right to enhance the rent and was entitled only to the capitalized value of the rent attributable to the acquired land; the remainder of the compensation was payable to the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the terms of the permanent lease as sanctioned under section 5 of the Bombay Hereditary Offices Act, 1874: the rent was fixed, and the Government’s order modified the rent without altering the other terms. Accordingly, the landlord’s interest in the acquired land was limited to the capitalized value of the rent. The Court did not rely on an earlier case for this substantive holding.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_apportionment_pro: The proceeding determined how compensation for compulsorily acquired land should be divided between the landlord and tenant.
predicates.permanent_lease_with_fixed_rent: The land was held under a permanent lease fixing the rent.
predicates.government_sanction_changed_only_rent: The Government sanctioned a revised rent without changing the lease’s other terms.
predicates.landlord_share_limited_to_capitalized_va: The landlord’s compensation share is limited to the capitalized value of the rent attributable to the acquired land.

issues.definition: In a compulsory-acquisition apportionment proceeding, a landlord under a permanent lease with fixed rent whose other terms were unchanged by government sanction receives only the capitalized value of the rent.
